_meta.purpose: Crypto ETF ACCESS routes reachable from Singapore, and the domicile/situs consequence of each. Deliberately SEPARATE from curated.json and from the scored ETF universe: these products carry no forward return, no volatility, no Efficiency Score, and no place in cma.json or model_portfolios.json. The page states which route is structurally cleaner for a Singapore holder; it takes no view on whether to hold crypto at all.
_meta.why_no_forward_return: The Expected returns tab is built on long-run capital market assumptions per asset class. No defensible long-run CMA exists for bitcoin or ether — published CMAs from major asset managers do not carry one, and inventing a number to fill the column would undermine every other figure on that tab. The columns are therefore left blank on purpose, not for want of data.
_meta.cost_basis_warning: Cost figures below are NOT all on the same basis. A management fee is not an ongoing charges figure, and an ongoing charges figure that is an ESTIMATE is not an actual one. Each record states its own basis in cost_basis and must be displayed with it. Comparing a 0.60% management fee against a 1.72% actual ongoing charges figure as though they were like-for-like would be wrong.
_meta.hk_counter_convention: HK crypto ETFs list multiple counters over one fund: 3xxx = HKD, 9xxx = USD, 83xxx = RMB. Same fund, same ISIN, different trading currency. A Singapore buyer holding USD generally uses the 9xxx counter and avoids one FX conversion.

situs_states.outside_us: The security held is a share in a non-US fund. Not US-situs on the same reasoning that makes an Irish UCITS fund not US-situs to its holder.
situs_states.unresolved: Situs is not settled. Shown as unresolved, never as safe. This site does not label an instrument estate-tax safe on inference.

_meta.verification_note: Figures marked ter_conf 'high' were read from the issuer filing named in src. 'med' means a single or secondary source and no current Key Facts Statement was reachable at the as-at date. No figure here is presented as audited where it is not.
_meta.sgx_route: There is no SGX-listed spot crypto ETF. Verified directly against this repo's own SGX ETF Screener export (data/sgx_etf_screener.csv, downloaded 2026-07-09): zero crypto entries. MAS has consistently stated that cryptocurrencies are not suitable for retail investors and has not authorised a spot crypto ETF for retail offer in Singapore.
_meta.ucits_route: There is no crypto UCITS ETF and there structurally cannot be one: crypto is not an eligible asset under the UCITS Directive, and a single-asset fund fails the diversification requirement regardless. ESMA's June 2025 technical advice to the Commission would admit crypto only inside a capped bucket of otherwise-ineligible assets; it is advice, it is non-binding, and it is not law. European crypto products are therefore ETPs / ETNs — debt securities, not funds.

routes.label: Hong Kong listed
routes.verdict: The only route that is both a fund and outside US situs.
routes.cost_note: You pay for the clean wrapper: roughly 0.6% to 1.7% a year against 0.25% on the US route.

routes.label: US listed
routes.wrapper: Delaware statutory trust (grantor trust for US income tax)
routes.verdict: Cheapest and deepest, with an estate-tax question the issuer itself declines to answer.
routes.cost_note: 0.25% sponsor fee on the two largest funds.

routes.label: European ETP / ETN
routes.wrapper: Debt security issued by a non-US issuer, physically collateralised
routes.verdict: Avoids a US issuer, but it is a note rather than a fund — the same reason this site declines to call gold ETCs situs-safe.
routes.cost_note: Cheapest headline fee of the three, but the wrapper is the trade-off.

products.name: iShares Bitcoin ETP
products.structure: Exchange-traded product — a DEBT SECURITY issued by a Swiss issuer, physically collateralised with bitcoin. Not a UCITS fund and not a fund at all.
products.src: justETF product profile and issuer listing data: ISIN XS2940466316, TER 0.15% p.a., Swiss-domiciled, issued by iShares Digital Assets AG, launched 18 March 2025, physically backed. Sources conflict on whether the 0.15% is promotional and steps up to 0.25% — one contemporaneous report at launch said it would rise by end-2025, the current product profile still shows 0.15%. Verify against the issuer factsheet before relying on it.

also_listed.note: The Hong Kong crypto ETF market has widened beyond the original April 2024 bitcoin and ether launches. ChinaAMC listed a spot Solana ETF (3460 HKD / 9460 USD / 83460 RMB) in October 2025 — Asia's first. It is named here for completeness of the route, not researched or listed as a product above, and carries no verified fee figure on this page.
